sections.sectionTitle: Section A: Language (Asụsụ / Fonetiki na Grama)

topics.title: Comprehension, Essay Writing, Sound System, Grammar, and Translation

subtopics.content: Reading passages, essay writing types, Igbo phonemes, syllable structure, sound processes (vowel harmony, elision), tones, spelling rules, word formation, standard Igbo vs dialects, word classes, grammatical categories, sentence types, direct/indirect speech, and translation
subtopics.objective: Answer comprehension questions on written Igbo passages; compose 300-word essays (narrative, argumentative, debate, letters) using standard metalanguage; describe Igbo vowels, consonants, syllabic nasals, vowel harmony, assimilation, and tone notation; apply spelling rules, identify loan words, and master word classes, tenses, phrases, clauses, sentence constituents, and speech forms; translate correctly between English and Igbo.

topics.title: Literary Appreciation, Oral Literature, and Written Literature

subtopics.content: Literary appreciation devices, oral literature genres (Ifo, Ukabuilu, Akụkọ Dike, Mbem, Ejije ọnụ), and prescribed written texts (prose, poetry, drama)
subtopics.objective: Apply literary appreciation techniques; examine oral literature genres, definitions, and functions; analyze prescribed oral literature texts (*Mbe Agaba*, *Abụ Agụrụnọnụ Ndị Igbo*); critique prescribed written prose (*Jụọ Obinna*); evaluate set written drama (*Otụ Mkpịsị Aka*); analyze selected written poems from *Akọnụche*.

subtopics.content: Igbo identity, greetings, hospitality (Ọjị, Ịgọ Ọfọ), birth rites, reincarnation/Ogbanje, festivals (Ịwa Ji, Ofala, Akwamọzụ), traditional games, taboos (Nsoala/Arụ), governance structures (Eze, Nze na Ọzọ, Umuada), social institutions, titles, traditional occupations, religious worship, and deities
subtopics.objective: Analyze Igbo identity, dress, greetings, and hospitality rites (Ọjị, Ịgọ Ọfọ); examine life-cycle rites (Omụgwo, naming, funerals) and beliefs (Ilo ụwa, Ogbanje); describe festivals (Ịwa Ji, Ofala) and traditional sports (Mgba, Ọkọsọ); detail taboos (Nsoala); evaluate governance bodies (Umụnna, Ụmụada, Nze na Ọzọ), chieftaincy titles, traditional crafts/occupations, divination, and traditional deities (Ala, Amadịoha, Ikenga).
